svg.text: Set the pattern in the stroke that cannot be faked.
Read it in the stroke that can. Repair at the slip, not at the end.
Swim fly, then freestyle with no rest between them. The freestyle inherits the chain, and that pairing is the method.
A functional concept is a confinement.
the midline, and your long axis

water it acts on, and the pressure collapses. A curved
path keeps meeting water that has not been accelerated.

destroys the sweep and leaves the push.

Relative to your body the hand travels a long curved path.
Relative to the water its net rearward travel is small. The deck
sees the second and calls it an anchor.
in fly the two coincide by construction
The report arrives every cycle. The commitment is one act
covering an extent: the length, and the wall that ends it.
fly: two mirrored question marks, the keyhole
freestyle: the same scull, one side at a time
and the roll does what symmetry did in fly
Fly, then free, no wall and no rest between them.
Keep the fly short. It sets the pattern, it is not the set.
Insert the fly at the onset of the slip, not at the end.
End the set when re-entry stops holding for a length.
Attend to pressure, acceleration, and the downkick.
25 fly, 15 m, six strokes, two, one, none.

A buoy confines too, and leaves arm-only as the only way
through. Paddles raise the threshold. Economy targets need a
speed floor, or coasting satisfies them.
how far into the set it survives
fly needed to restore it, 25 to one stroke
Open cold with body dolphins, then sculling, then easy
fly. Never loose limbs, which ask the trunk for nothing.
Warm with no prime is the proof it is installed.

A fly that must be muscled can be brute-forced for 25 and
enforces nothing. Build it first, ratcheting as it gets
Or breaststroke with a clear dolphin: first downbeat on the
outsweep, second as the hands shoot forward, head with the
spine. Weaker, so expect a shorter carry.
Cues, one per set, never stacked
“keep the water packed on the forearm”
Retired: “move past your anchored hand”, and “over the
barrel”, which names the drape and not the action. “Don’t
let the hand move” holds only at set. Never trace the S.
Recovery names a target, never a shape.
Observables from the deck, in the order they go
The question mark flattens toward a straight line. The outsweep goes first, so the
hand drops and travels back instead of sweeping out.
Force starts later in the cycle. From the side you see a slip, then a shove. Watch
when the pressure starts, not where the hand is.
Quiet and flat, roll amplitude down, roll shoulder-led. Most reliable tell. Hips
that sink are a different fault: balance, not the chain.
The downbeat no longer punctuates the outsweep. The kick drifts to random phase,
The stroke gets louder mid-length. Listen rather than watch; slip is audible
A boil alongside the hip means water pushed backwards. Bubbles shed in a trail
behind you are vortices left where the sweeps turned.
Hand starts leading, arm straightens, elbow drops, entry slaps. The body has
A flat dead moment at the hand exit, because the swimmer waits for the next pull
Head creeping up, chin tucking, a lift to air instead of a roll, and the breath
Stroke count lags. Distance per stroke holds while the cost climbs, and tempo hides it. Side video at hip height settles the hip and the path in one length.
Log the reversion, do not name it. Naming the fault mid-length installs the examiner. Call the distance, “you went at 60”, and insert one fly stroke.
Fly is a staircase. Push the step away, commit to the line, and arrive.
A transaction has a beginning and an extent. A cue has neither.
